title: CI job runner with atomic admission control
name: CI job runner pool

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code enforces the concurrency limit and updates its shared counters? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
An operator calls the reload endpoint, which lowers MaxConcurrent and JobTimeout, while several jobs are mid-run. What happens to those in-flight jobs?
choices: They are cancelled immediately because the new limits no longer allow them
They keep running but their timeout is re-evaluated against the new JobTimeout on the next tick
They keep running with the Limits pointer they were started with, including the old timeout; only later submissions see the new values
The reload blocks until running reaches zero, then swaps the pointer

questions.prompt: Snapshot reads Succeeded, Failed and TotalNanos with separate atomic loads. What can a caller of Snapshot observe?
choices: A mean run time computed from counters sampled at slightly different moments, so it can be marginally off, but each value is a valid whole number
A torn int64 value on 32-bit platforms, since the loads are independent
A data race that the Go race detector would report
A panic from division by zero whenever a job finishes between the loads

questions.prompt: The HTTP handler passes r.Context() to Submit, and the client disconnects right after receiving 202 Accepted. What happens to the job?
choices: It is cancelled, because the job context derives from the request context
It is cancelled only if the client disconnects before the goroutine starts
It keeps running, but without any deadline since the request context is dropped
It keeps running; context.WithoutCancel detaches it from the request's cancellation while keeping its values, and only JobTimeout can stop it
